assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints that amplify and propagate shocks are a core mechanism in modern macro-finance. The framework underpins research on financial frictions, firm borrowing against asset values, and crisis models. Its reach into corporate finance, banking and policy analysis is broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore (credit cycles) and Gertler, with Bernanke and Gilchrist (financial accelerator), are the clearest intellectual core. Bernanke already shared the 2022 prize for banking and financial crises, so the financial accelerator is partly acknowledged. I therefore weight Kiyotaki-Moore most heavily. Gilchrist is more empirical and extension work and is left out to respect the three-name limit.
assessment.maturity: The foundational papers date from the 1990s, so there has been ample time for confirmation. The 2008 crisis and later work confirmed the relevance of the mechanisms. This is mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize may lead some members to see the area as already honoured.
Whether Gertler belongs in the same trio, given his joint work with the 2022 laureate Bernanke.
Empirical identification of the quantitative size of collateral channels remains debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The firm-heterogeneity framework changed trade theory and empirics. It explains exporter selection, within-industry reallocation and a new channel for gains from trade. It underlies a large body of quantitative and micro-data work and has had real policy influence.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution. Helpman has broad earlier contributions to new trade theory plus firm-level work, notably Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on FDI versus exports. Redding is important on quantitative spatial and trade models but is more of a follower and extender. Krugman's 2008 prize covered new trade theory, which is related but distinct.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation across many countries' firm-level data. The theory is mature and widely taught.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as sufficiently distinct from the 2008 trade prize.
Helpman's contribution is wide-ranging, which complicates how the citation would be framed, and Eaton-Kortum and Bernard-Jensen work also deserve credit.
Debate over the welfare gains attributable specifically to selection.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: These authors established a modern, formal and empirically testable political economics. They analyse how electoral rules and constitutions shape fiscal policy, redistribution and state capacity. The work links directly to comparative development and public finance, and it systematically brought political institutions into mainstream economics.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini (Political Economics, constitutional and electoral rules) are the clearest intellectual core. Besley (state capacity, accountability, political agency) is a major complementary contributor. The three-name proposal is reasonable and consistent, though other contributors exist.
assessment.maturity: The central work dates from the 1990s and 2000s and has been extensively tested, with empirical tests of constitutional effects accumulating. The 2024 prize recognised institutions and prosperity, so the area has recent Nobel attention, but the topic here is distinct.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2024 institutions prize may weigh against, or for, the field.
Identification problems in cross-country constitutional comparisons.
Torsten Persson's past committee role may raise conflict questions, which are disclosed but not adjudicated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work links household leverage and credit supply to housing booms, consumption collapses and unemployment. It reshaped views of the Great Recession and the macroeconomics of credit cycles, built on large-scale micro data. It has influenced policy debates on debt restructuring and financial regulation.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the clear joint originators of the household-debt and credit-supply empirical program. Campbell is a major finance scholar (household finance, asset pricing), but his credit is less tied to this discovery, so I leave him out.
assessment.maturity: Key papers date from about 2009 to 2014, so a decade or more of replication and extension exists. Maturity is good but less than for the older candidates.
uncertainties: Debate over causal interpretation of the credit-supply shock and the demand-versus-supply channels.
Some elements of the story involve earlier theory (Kiyotaki-Moore, Minsky, Fisher), which could dilute novelty.
Timing relative to the 2022 banking-crises prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities is the working core of modern monetary policy analysis in central banks. Contributions include staggered pricing and contracts, policy rules, and the micro-founded synthesis. The practical influence on policy practice is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Calvo (staggered pricing), Taylor (staggered contracts and the Taylor rule) and Woodford (synthesis and optimal policy) are the strongest credits. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans and Smets-Wouters are important but more in the estimation and extension branch. The pool of credit is wide and contested, and many deserving people fall outside three names.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature. The framework has been used for decades, though its performance after 2008 and in the 2021-23 inflation episode prompted reassessment.
uncertainties: Attribution is diffuse and any three-person selection will be contested.
Some prior Nobel recognition of rational expectations and macro methodology (Lucas, Sargent, Kydland-Prescott, Phelps) overlaps conceptually.
Debate over the model's empirical adequacy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This line of work established how technology, tasks and import competition reshape labour demand, wages and local labour markets. The China-shock evidence changed the trade and political-economy debate, and the task framework changed labour economics. Both are policy-relevant and widely cited.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the common thread across the task and trade-shock literatures. Hanson (with Dorn and Autor) is central to the trade shock. Katz is central to the education-technology race and the inequality literature. Dorn is a close co-author on the China shock but is left out because of the three-name cap. The Acemoglu-Restrepo task-automation work was partly recognised in the 2024 prize.
assessment.maturity: The task approach dates from about 2003 and the China-shock evidence from 2013 onward. Replication is substantial, but the long-run adjustment and welfare conclusions are still being debated.
uncertainties: Katz appears on another ballot item, which affects how credit is distributed across the field.
The long-run persistence of trade-shock effects and the role of automation versus trade.
Partial overlap with the 2021 and 2024 prizes in labour and technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The law-and-finance program placed legal institutions and investor protection at the center of cross-country financial development and corporate governance. It created a large literature and shaped policy. The corporate-finance dimension of the work is of direct interest and influence.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny formed the original four-author team. Shleifer is the most prominent and has broader contributions in behavioral finance and corporate governance. The three-name limit forces an exclusion of Vishny, which is hard to defend on attribution alone.
assessment.maturity: The work is from 1997 onward, with a long record of follow-up. The long record also includes serious methodological critiques, which are part of the assessment.
uncertainties: Replication and measurement critiques of the legal-origins indicators and the legal-origin identification strategy.
Excluding Vishny from the trio is a significant attribution judgment.
Potential reputational and other non-scientific considerations around some candidates, which I treat only as uncertainty and not as an adjudicated matter.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation research quantified how distortions in resource allocation across firms explain large cross-country TFP and income differences. It opened a very active research program in macro-development and had clear policy relevance for understanding productivity gaps.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) are the central authors. Restuccia and Rogerson (2008), who are not credited in this ballot item as Rogerson, are an important parallel contribution. Restuccia is credited here, but I limit the proposal to the two authors most closely tied to the quantitative approach, and the omission of Restuccia is a judgment.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen or more years of follow-up. There is a lot of confirmation of the qualitative idea, though the measurement of misallocation is contested.
uncertainties: Measurement error and the interpretation of dispersion in marginal products as distortions.
Parallel contribution by Restuccia-Rogerson complicates attribution.
Newer than the other macro candidates, so the long-run influence is less established.
